original_fields.Title: Labour market statistics (income) – description
original_fields.Content: Labour market statistics (income) reports on information about income collected annually from the Household Labour Force Survey (HLFS). It provides information about individual and household income, including wages and salaries, self-employment, and government transfers income, both at an aggregate level and for subpopulations of interest.

original_fields.Title: Labour market statistics (income): June 2026 quarter – key facts 1
original_fields.Content:
Key facts

In the June 2026 quarter, compared with the June 2025 quarter, median weekly income from:

  • all sources was $962, compared with $959
  • wages and salaries was $1,419, up $38 (2.8 percent)
  • self-employment was $959, compared with $921
  • government transfers was $486, up $15 (3.1 percent).

Median hourly earnings from wages and salaries increased by $0.96 (2.7 percent) to $35.96 in the year to the June 2026 quarter.

The gender pay gap was 5.3 percent in the June 2026 quarter, compared with 5.2 percent in the June 2025 quarter. This remains lower than the June 2024 quarter, when the gender pay gap was 8.2 percent.

All income data refers to gross (before tax) income for individuals.

Income from all sources collected

Median weekly income from all sources collected, for all people, was $962 in the June 2026 quarter (compared with $959 in the June 2025 quarter).

original_fields.Title: Labour market statistics (income): June 2026 quarter – key facts 2
original_fields.Content:
Median weekly income from all sources collected comprises income from wages and salaries, self-employment, government transfers, and ACC. It includes people with negative or no income.

Wages and salaries

Median weekly earnings

Median weekly earnings from wages and salaries were $1,419 in the June 2026 quarter, an increase of $38 (2.8 percent) from $1,381 in the June 2025 quarter.

  • For men, median weekly earnings were $1,538, an increase of $38 (2.5 percent) from $1,500 in the June 2025 quarter.
  • For women, median weekly earnings were $1,280, an increase of $33 (2.7 percent) from $1,247 in the June 2025 quarter.

original_fields.Title: Labour market statistics (income): June 2026 quarter – key facts 4
original_fields.Content:
Full-time median hourly earnings were $38.00 in the June 2026 quarter, an increase of $1.44 (3.9 percent) from $36.56 in the June 2025 quarter.

Part-time hourly earnings were $28.49, an increase of $0.99 (3.6 percent) from $27.50.

In the year to the June 2026 quarter, median hourly earnings from wages and salaries also increased for the following ethnic groups:

  • Māori – up $1.45 (4.5 percent) to $33.45
  • European – up $1.41 (3.9 percent) to $37.85
  • Asian – up $0.96 (2.9 percent) to $33.56.

For Pacific peoples, median hourly earnings from wages and salaries were $31.17 in the June 2026 quarter.

Government transfers

Median weekly income from government transfers increased by $15 (3.1 percent) to $486 in the year to the June 2026 quarter.

Government transfers include income from New Zealand Superannuation, Veteran’s Pension, Student Allowance, and transfers from Inland Revenue, and Work and Income.

Disability

In the June 2026 quarter, compared with the June 2025 quarter, median weekly income for disabled people from:

  • all sources was $527, compared with $518
  • wages and salaries was $1170, compared with $1163
  • government transfers was $495, compared with $488.

Gender pay gap at 5.3 percent

The gender pay gap was at 5.3 percent in the June 2026 quarter, compared with 5.2 percent the previous year. This means that, on average, women earned 5.3 percent less for an hour’s work than men.

The gender pay gap is calculated using median hourly wage and salary earnings for men and women. Changes to median pay are more representative of pay changes for most workers than changes to mean (average) pay.

original_fields.Title: LMSI June 2026 qtr – g4 – Gender pay gap (%), June quarters, 1998–2026
Labour market statistics (income): June 2026 quarter – key facts 5
original_fields.Content:
Data for this release comes from the Household Labour Force Survey (HLFS). As the HLFS is a sample survey, and does not interview every person in New Zealand, a small amount of uncertainty is expected for any estimates produced. This uncertainty is often represented as sample errors, which show the bounds of confidence an estimate lies in. Sampling errors can be used to understand whether a genuine (or statistically significant) change has occurred.

With an estimate of 5.3 percent, the gender pay gap had a sampling error of about 1.7 percentage points in the June 2026 quarter. This means we are largely confident that the gender pay gap lies between 3.6 and 7.1 percent.

Working-class heroes: Understanding labour market data has more information on sampling errors and confidence intervals.

A gender pay gap of 0 percent would imply no difference in earnings between men and women. This measure does not consider factors that could influence differences in earnings, such as occupation, qualifications gained, age, and hours worked.

Measuring the gender pay gap has more information on gender pay gaps, how to calculate them, and why we use median pay.

Organisational gender pay gaps: Measurement and analysis guidelines explains how to calculate the gender pay gap within your own organisation.

Gender pay gap toolkit is a resource provided by the Ministry for Women including a tool to calculate the gender pay gap within your organisation.
